cohort: The study included 220 postnatal mothers who delivered live infants via vaginal or cesarean delivery at a tertiary care hospital during a 3-month period.
finding: Early breastfeeding initiation was observed in 71% of mothers, with the most common reason for delayed initiation being the baby admitted to the NICU after delivery (50%).
cross-section timing: Data was collected on postnatal mothers while they were still in the hospital after delivery, focusing on early breastfeeding initiation.
